clue.text: Fuel exporters 'ave confidence on taking cocaine

parts.note: confidence is hope; written with the H dropped, as the apostrophe in 'ave signals
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: Oil-producing nations, drawled in Cockney, are buoyed up by a line of coke.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'ave tells you to drop the H of the synonym too.
explanation.definitionFit: OPEC is the cartel of petroleum-producing countries, so its members export fuel.

clue.text: Local creep and piss-artist's perambulations

parts.note: in Britain your local is the pub nearest home
to creep is to crawl

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood sneak and a drunk go for their strolls.
explanation.walkthrough: A piss-artist is British slang for a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub crawl is a drinking tour from bar to bar, exactly the wandering a habitual drunk does.

clue.text: In the process of screwing someone you've taken out? Change to the latest version

parts.note: vulgar slang: to be up someone is to be having sex with them
the person you take out for the evening is your date

explanation.surface: A crude question about bedding the person you took to dinner, followed by an unrelated software instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To update something is to revise it so it reflects the newest state.

clue.text: Spot the solicitor with foreign article

parts.note: a pimp solicits for clients, so he is a solicitor in the street sense
le is the French definite article

explanation.surface: Pick out the lawyer accompanied by a piece of writing from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a solicitor is a kind of lawyer, which is the reading the surface wants; here it is a man who solicits.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimple is a small inflamed bump on the skin, which is one sense of a spot.

clue.text: Beginnings of anti terror legislation stunt (double-crossed on return flight from UK to US)

definitions.text: double-crossed on return flight from UK to US

indicators.note: beginnings are the opening letters, so take the first letter of each following word

parts.note: the initial letters of these three words
an antic is a playful stunt or caper

explanation.surface: A sneer at security theatre: new terror laws turn a transatlantic round trip into an ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is the definition: a there-and-back flight between Britain and America crosses this ocean twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic Ocean lies between the UK and the US, so a return trip crosses it once each way.

clue.text: Act as if you've come to please a man

definitions.text: Act as if you've come to please a man

parts.note: surface reading: pretend you have just arrived somewhere
setter's reading: feign a climax in bed to flatter a male partner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Come' looks like arrival but is the sexual sense; the whole clue describes the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to simulate something, especially an orgasm, without truly experiencing it.

clue.text: Gore ready to provide the assassin's reward?

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
the ready is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: Al Gore stands prepared to pay off a hitman.
explanation.walkthrough: Gore looks like the US politician; it is just blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood money is the payment made to a hired killer for a murder.

clue.text: Overweight Prescott's main protuberance

indicators.note: the main part of a name is taken here as its head, the leading letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the name
a lump is a swelling that sticks out

explanation.surface: A jibe at portly John Prescott's chief bulge.
explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott was Tony Blair's heavyset Deputy Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump is a gentle word for carrying too much weight.

clue.text: Is not commonly inserted in soft testicle for pseudo-military sport

indicators.note: something inserted in is put inside the words that follow

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical mark for soft
ain't is the colloquial form of is not
ball is slang for a testicle

explanation.surface: Bad grammar crammed into a limp body part to make a war game.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintball is a combat game in which players shoot each other with pellets of dye.

clue.text: Tart re-applying dung dip

indicators.note: applying the letters again in a new way means rearranging them

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A floozy reapplies her make-up in a muck bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Tart looks like a loose woman; here it is a baked dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart is a sweet pastry dish, and a pudding is the British word for any dessert course.

clue.text: (& 20ac.) Turn up with tossers like Jeffrey Archer, politically — and one of his fictional creations?

parts.note: to cock a hat or an ear is to turn it up
with means together with, hence and
bulls toss people on their horns
Jeffrey Archer was a Conservative peer

explanation.surface: A sneer at Archer and his Tory chums, with a dig at his inventions.
explanation.walkthrough: Tossers looks like British slang abuse; here it means animals that toss. Archer, a novelist, was jailed for perjury over a false alibi, so his fictions went beyond his books.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock-and-bull story is an implausible made-up tale, and Archer's invented alibi was just such a lie.

clue.text: Pretend drug gets to fix stinking problem

parts.note: to fix something is to place it in position
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: Someone hopes a sham medicine will cure their smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is an inert dummy treatment given as if it were real medicine.

clue.text: Not warmonger Bush's favourite puff

parts.note: surface reading: some smoke George W Bush would not choose, as a man bent on war
setter's reading: the smoke is the ceremonial one shared to seal a truce, the opposite of war

explanation.walkthrough: Bush is George W Bush, who led the Iraq invasion; the smoke a warmonger would least enjoy is the one that ends fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A peace pipe is the calumet smoked by Native American leaders to confirm a treaty.

clue.text: Rotary club is pits for the likes of Max Clifford

indicators.note: rotary means turning round, so the letters are spun into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dig that Rotary Club gatherings are dire for celebrity spin doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotary looks like the service club; it only tells you to turn the letters. Max Clifford was a notorious British tabloid PR agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Clifford sold stories and managed press coverage for clients, which is the trade of publicity agents.

clue.text: Cyclops, given drink, totally flips — it's symbolic

indicators.note: flipping the whole thing over turns the combined letters end to end

parts.note: the setter Cyclops refers to himself, so me
a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: The setter gets a drink and goes completely mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops is the setter's pseudonym, so it stands for me.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or emblem that stands as a symbol for a clan or idea.

clue.text: Bollocks follow such a sturdy pet?

parts.note: both are slang for nonsense
to dog someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: An exasperated question whether a stocky dog will chase after things.
explanation.walkthrough: Bollocks reads as an expletive; it means nonsense, as does bull.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulldog is a squat, muscular breed often kept as a family companion.

clue.text: Assume your audience is thick, inarticulate and depressed

parts.note: dumb means unable to speak
feeling down is feeling low

explanation.surface: A list of the qualities a contemptuous broadcaster imagines in viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes thick, inarticulate and depressed look like one list; the first item belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dumb down is to simplify content on the assumption that the public cannot cope with more.

clue.text: Political dissenters: "F*** doing anything!"

parts.note: the asterisks leave just the initial letter of the swear word
action is doing something

explanation.surface: Rebel party members shrug off any initiative with a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a splinter group within a party, often one opposing its leadership.

clue.text: Smooth writer groped breast — time to be usurped by Penny

indicators.note: a usurper takes the place of the rightful holder, so one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: groped means felt with the hands
slang for a breast
T is the abbreviation for time
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A slick author's sexual assault, with a woman named Penny stepping in.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a woman's name; it is the coin. The last T of the breast word gives way to P.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tip pen glides easily over paper, so it is a smooth-writing instrument.

clue.text: Got up Princess Royal, roughly around end of night (excessive reverence)

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: Princess Diana, a standard crossword princess

indicators.note: around means wrapped about the outside of another piece
roughly means approximately, so these letters are not in exact order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Anne, the Princess Royal, gets up and dresses late at night for adoring crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Royal is the title of Princess Anne, but the clue splits it: Princess alone gives Diana's DI.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is worship of idols, and figuratively any blind, excessive devotion.

clue.text: A religion demonstrates "Cyclops rubbish!"

parts.note: the setter Cyclops speaking of himself
to rubbish something is to slam it with criticism

explanation.surface: A faith publicly declares the setter's work worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: Rubbish looks like a noun for junk; it is the verb meaning to run down.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic faith founded on the Qur'an.

clue.text: Feel bad about sticking it up Dave Spart?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, so backwards
the outer letters stand about the piece that is stuck in among them
bad signals the letters before it are spoilt, put into a corrupted order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
taken as written

explanation.surface: Guilt at needling the Eye's resident ranter.
explanation.walkthrough: Dave Spart is Private Eye's long-running parody of a ranting far-left student activist, so the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Spart is the caricature of a hard-left militant, and leftie is the informal word for such a socialist.

clue.text: see 10ac.
Henry and co. plotted to get head from her? "Only be kinky"

definitions.text: Henry and co. plotted to get head from her?

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so these letters are bent out of their order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A smutty joke about a king's sexual demands, with her reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting head looks like oral sex; it is a beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Boleyn, second wife of Henry VIII, was condemned on trumped-up charges and beheaded in 1536.

clue.text: Set about getting woman hot and damp

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone sets about seducing a woman, with predictable heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy describes air that is warm and humid, and also anything erotically charged.

clue.text: Muslim's take on Christian working in deli taking in female?

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so one piece is placed within the other
letters that are working are moving about, so they rearrange

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A Christian takes a job behind a delicatessen counter and hires a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Infidel, meaning unbeliever, is the term a devout Muslim might apply to a Christian.

clue.text: The ones concealing criminal charge get the treatment

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: they means those ones
a rap is a criminal charge, as in a murder rap

explanation.surface: Those hiding a criminal charge end up roughed up.
explanation.walkthrough: Get the treatment sounds like being beaten up; the definition is the medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment intended to heal an illness or disorder.

clue.text: Abominable sort of Eye tip: "ignore Express political leaders"

indicators.note: to ignore letters is to leave them out

parts.note: taken as written; that the wanted letters already run inside these words is a coincidence of the deletion, which names the outer two to strip

indicators.note: leaders are the front-runners, so take the opening letter of each word

parts.note: the initial letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Private Eye's tip: disregard the Daily Express's political pundits, who are dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Express is a British tabloid. Remove the first E and the P from the six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti of the Himalayas is popularly known as the Abominable Snowman.

clue.text: One getting stuck into pisspoor, pushy twat endlessly seen on the box?

indicators.note: to be stuck into something is to be lodged inside it
something pisspoor is badly done, so these letters are in a poor order
without its end means the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, once trimmed
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone lays into a feeble, obnoxious TV presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: Seen on the box looks like appearing on television; it means printed on a cardboard carton.
explanation.definitionFit: This way up is the instruction stencilled on parcels so they are kept the right way round.

clue.text: Desert Frenchman's main word for "sex"

parts.note: mer is French for the sea, and the main is the open sea
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: An abandoned Frenchman's chief euphemism for sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert looks like a verb or a sandy waste; it is the noun in getting your just deserts.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert is something deserved, and merit is the quality of deserving reward.
